title.narrative: Humanitarian and emergency action for victims of the rains in Rodeio City, in the state of Santa Cat

description.narrative: Since December 2022, several regions of the Santa Catarina State where it usually rains between 150 mm and 200 mm in the period, were recorded a volume three times higher than average. During this period, according to a survey published by the State Government, 17 municipalities suffered damage and two declared a state of emergency. Consequently, on the night of 17 January 2023, a torrential rain fell in the city of Rodeio (Located in the Itajaí Valley, 186 km from Florianópolis and has an area of 135 square kilometres and 11,488 inhabitants), causing significant damage. The municipality declared a state of public calamity on Wednesday (18). Many people have lost everything in their houses. Again, at the beginning of February the warning of heavy rains happened again in the Itajaí Valley, the rain of Thursday night (2) and early morning of Friday left homeless, flooded houses and blocked streets, especially for the vulnerability that caused by the previous rain. The aim of this project is to enable vulnerable families affected by the floods in Rodeio to meet their basic needs and to succeed in restoring their lives both materially and psychologically. The dioceses chosen for this project is Diocesan Cáritas of Rio do Sul due to the proximity and the need for immediate response. Considering this general objective, the following intervention will be developed: For CASH, the project aims to assist 118 households with multipurpose cards. Distribution of unrestricted and unconditional multipurpose cards will allow families to choose the items and materials they most need at the time. Among these 118 families that will be contemplated by the project, it was identified through a rapid assessment together with the Diocese of Rio do Sul that 38 had lost everything in their homes, and, therefore, received a larger amount than the other 80 families that had partial losses. Therefore, common to both groups of families, the following needs were identified during the assessment: 1) food security, 2) non-food items (NFI) and 3) Hygiene items (WASH). As for the group that lost everything and still had damages to their homes, an amount will be included for the purchase and reestablishment of their homes, according to the 4) Shelter norms, enabling people to establish shelter and housing that meet their individual and collective needs.
